subject: QBR capacity & unit-econ prep: infra GPU spend, utilization, batching/caching impacts
content:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karen Li <karen@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: infra capacity & unit-econ prep - data request

Team —

As we lock slides for the QBR next week, I want a concise section on infra capacity and unit economics that the ELT can act on. Specifically I need:

- 2–3 headline metrics for GPU spend this quarter vs. last (absolute $ and $/1M tokens served)
- Average GPU utilization across pools (hosted vs dedicated) and slot-level bottlenecks
- Quantified impact of batching and prefix/KV caching on effective tokens and cost per request (best and typical cases)
- Any one-off capacity events / overprovisioning we should call out

Can you each own a piece: Dev, pull the raw cost & utilization numbers and a short table of batching/caching delta scenarios. Laura, draft two slides: one showing spend + utilization trend, second showing a simple decision matrix for when to use dedicated vs hosted and expected unit-econ impact. Evelyn, include any SLAs/ops flags we should mention.

Please drop a spreadsheet and a short PDF summary into the QBR folder by Monday EOD. Also include a short note on assumptions (e.g., token definition, amortized HW vs OPEX split).

Thanks — Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Karen Li <karen@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: infra capacity & unit-econ prep - data request

Marcus —

Attached is a concise workbook (qbr_infra_costs_2026Q2.xlsx) and a short PDF summary (batching-impact-summary.pdf). Highlights below:

- GPU spend: $1.73M this quarter vs $1.32M last quarter (+31%). Incremental spend driven by two factors: model mix shift to longer-context customers (~+12%) and temporary burst capacity for Region-us-east (~+9%).
- $/1M tokens served (hosted, weighted avg): $225 (this quarter) vs $190 (prior). Dedicated pools show $/1M tokens of $165 but require 60% utilization to break even vs hosted.
- Average GPU utilization: hosted pools 38% (wide variance by route), dedicated pools 62% (skewed by two big customers). Tail latency incidents correlate with <20% utilization on inference slots during low-traffic windows, indicating overprovisioning for warm caches.
- Batching/caching impact (conservative vs optimistic):
  - Conservative: batching reduces GPU token cost by ~15%; prefix/KV caching reduces active compute by ~10% (net ~23% cost saving when both applied).
  - Optimistic (peak-friendly): batching + cache together can reduce per-token compute by up to ~35% for long-context, high-reuse workloads.

Notes & assumptions: tokens measured post-normalization; amortized HW cost includes depreciation and rack-level overhead; we excluded networking and egress for simplicity. Full calc tabs are in the workbook.

Attachments: qbr_infra_costs_2026Q2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 4 tabs: summary, by-pool, batching-sim, amortization)
batching-impact-summary.pdf (2 pages, charts + key takeaways)

Happy to walk through numbers Monday morning.

Cheers,
Dev

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Karen Li <karen@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: infra capacity & unit-econ prep - data request

Great work, Dev —/ grabbing the workbook now and drafting slides. A few quick editorial asks for ELT clarity:

- Slide 1 (headline): Waterfall chart showing spend delta (last Q -> this Q) with callouts for model-mix, burst capacity, and amortization change. Add two bullets: $/1M tokens (hosted) and $/1M tokens (dedicated @ current utilization).
- Slide 2 (decision matrix): Rows: customer size (small/med/enterprise), latency requirement (best-effort/low-latency), data-sensitivity (standard/regulated). Columns: recommended route (hosted/dedicated/private), expected unit-econ delta (%).
- Add a small inset table showing batching+cache conservative/optimistic lines (Dev's numbers).

I added a skeleton deck to the Drive (link below) and a working outline (qbr_slide_outline.pptx). If we can get one short quote from Karen about how caching affects their billing predictability, that would be perfect for the customer-case callout.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQBR-data
HubSpot note: HS-Deal-4257

Laura
Director, Growth & GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachment: qbr_slide_outline.pptx

From: Karen Li <karen@acmecloud.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: infra capacity & unit-econ prep - data request

Thanks for the context — happy to help. A quick clarification on caching: our billing model charges based on tokens served, but effective tokens for us drop materially when prefix caching is available because many requests hit a cached response and do not trigger inference compute. When you report the batching+cache % gains, please call out that our observed effective token reduction translates to lower variable spend but does not reduce committed reserved capacity (if dedicated). For the slide, a one-line customer quote: "Caching reduced our compute spend by ~22% during peak windows while keeping latency steady."

Karen Li
Head of ML Systems
Acuity Analytics
